articleTitle: Synchronization of Virtual and Real Learning Patterns in E-Learning Systems with Metaverse Concept
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This article aims to describe learning designs for synchronizing the real and virtual worlds. Learning Management System (LMS) is a learning manager and has become a common system. LMS has been used at various levels of education. In universities, LMS is often referred to as e-learning. The domination of content by lecturers needs to be reconstructed so that the learning resources developed by lecturers and students become optimal as a synchronization catalyst. The metaverse concept gives students access to construct learning resources independently. The results of the analysis show that students have an interest in learning about learning resources, which are developed by fellow students. Synergy between the real and virtual worlds can be combined through LMS with the concept of metaverse.

articleTitle: Improving Company Performance by The Correctness of Management Decision through Implementation Dashboard using Power BI Tools (Case Study at Company Y)
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Making the right decisions is one of the important things in supporting the performance of a company. Companies need good data analysis in order to produce insightful information that can be used as the basis for making the right decisions. Data needs to be extracted, processed and visualized on analytical panels (dashboard) so that it can be analyzed and become useful information for company management in making decisions. This paper is about dashboard implementation using Power BI (Business Intelligence) in a case study company Y. The goals is to understand how dashboard implementation using Power BI and improve business performance with precision management decisions that can help business enterprises to look back in history and assist with forward planning.

articleTitle: Bringing Computational Thinking Skills Into Physics Classroom Through Project-Based Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Computational thinking is a fundamental thinking skill for students in the 21st-century learning era. This study aims to integrate computational thinking skills in physics through project-based learning. Data were gathered through observation, interviews, and portfolio documents. The results indicated three main categories of computational thinking: decomposition, abstraction, and simulation. The implementation of project-based learning can develop students’ computational thinking skills. Students are trained to solve physics problems analytically and precisely in structured and logical thinking through a project. This research is expected to be the information for physics teachers to integrate computational thinking in the classroom as a 21st-century learning skill.

articleTitle: Mobile Live Coding Development as a Disruptive Learning Media in Programming Course
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Learning media is a tool that can help and support teaching and learning activities so that they can run well and smoothly. A good learning media can the meaning of the message more clearly including the flow of learning objectives, materials, evaluations, and even communication media, and practicum media. The mobile application in this study contains the flow of learning objectives as a reference for achieving learning objectives, text and videos, discussion forums as communication media, live coding media for practicum, and quizzes as evaluation material. The research method used is Research and Development (RnD) or development research. The development process uses the ADDIE method (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation). The problem in the introduction states that students have limitations in accessing learning resources, so using this application can increase student interest in learning. Using the live coding feature in this application can help students understand C++ programming and measure their understanding of the material contained in the mobile application. From the research conducted, that the average percentage of respondents after using the Sinau Coding application is 83,3% and it can be concluded that this application is valid and feasible criterion for use in the field of education.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality Implementation for Human Anatomy Learning in Medical Education: A Review
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic has changed the style of teaching and learning, one of them in medical education. Face-to-face meetings during the COVID-19 pandemic can no longer be done freely. With existing limitations, students are required to learn to understand learning without face-to-face with educators, especially medical students. So, it is necessary touse learning media that can increase active learning and learning independently. Learning media such as augmented reality is one that needs to be studied to help students learn. This research aims to understand the state-of-the-art of augmented reality implementation for human anatomy learning in the medical education field from 2018 to 2022. This research reviews recent studies about augmented implementation for human anatomy learning in medical education. The results of this research explain that there are things that can still be a challenge for further research. Future research can explore research for general people who use augmented reality to educate about human anatomy and the impact of its use. Another suggestion is to develop by minimizing the cost as low as possible.

articleTitle: Emotional Expressions Recognize Ability in Children with Autism: Intervention Using Emotion Recognition Assistance Application
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The ability to recognize emotional expression is the basis for developing social relationship skills. Children with autism spectrum disorders have difficulties in recognizing other people’s emotional expressions. In this study, an experiment was conducted to improve the skills of recognizing basic emotional expressions (angry, happy, sad and afraid) using assistive technology based on the Emotion Recognition Assistance (ERA) android application. There are three levels of activity interactively carried out by research subjects in the ERA application, namely recognizing basic emotions, matching emotional expressions with the context and finally imitating emotional expressions by taking photos of themselves to then be responded to by the system regarding the accuracy of emotional expressions shown. The results of data analysis with Wilcoxcon showed the results of a significant increase in skills between before and after treatment in 10 research subjects with ages between 10 and d. 17 years.

articleTitle: Optimizing Regression on Genetic Algorithms for Effective scheduling based on the Predicted Number of Students
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Scheduling courses is a routine job that every educational institution always carries out at the beginning of the semester. Scheduling is a complicated task because the scheduling problem is a combinatorial problem with limitations that must be met. These limits are divided into absolute limits that must be met, such as the availability of classrooms and their capacity, the availability of lecturers and students, and soft limitations, such as lecturers’ preference in teaching time. The best solution to the scheduling problem is to-predict the number of course takers in the next semester within a certain period. This research solves this problem by predicting the number of applicants for the next semester’s courses. This study uses a genetic algorithm to optimize the data and parameters obtained from the data of enthusiasts of previous courses. After optimizing the data, regression is carried out to predict the number of enthusiasts for the following semester’s courses. The results of this test show that MSE was 0.445138347 in 2020, and the error rate based on all accurate and predictive data is 14.34%.

articleTitle: Understanding the Continuance Behavior towards E-Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Performing users’ behavior analysis on elearning is very important for education, especially in formulating and developing a distance education platform with a better learning experience and can provide a more efficient and accurate evaluation of e-learning for continuing education. There are 20 recent studies in continuance behavior towards elearning from January 2018 to April 2022. To provide a more comprehensive overview of continuance behavior towards elearning, a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted. Three research question conducted to recognize and assess research methods and major theories used in continuance behavior towards e-learning, as well as identify factors that influence sustainable behavior towards elearning. 18 different basic theories (like TAM, TPB, ECM, UTAUT, etc.) or models with 92 kinds of factors were identified and seven factors were dominants to used in research about continuance behavior towards e-learning. The result show that there is one method that is suitable to be used as base model in research about continuance behavior towards e-learning. Most importantly, this study provides a theoretical basis for further research in this context.

articleTitle: Simulation of Low-Frequency Sine Wave Generator with DDS Method Based on Arduino Uno using SimulIDE Simulator
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: DDS (Direct Digital Synthesis) is a method to produce analog waves using digital techniques. Analog waves can be sine waves, square waves, triangular waves, or others. This research used SimulIDE simulator software to simulate electronic hardware or hardware, an Arduino Uno microcontroller, and Oscilloscope. This research utilized the PWM (Pulse With Modulation) feature on the Arduino Uno microcontroller, where the amount of duty cycle was regulated using the DDS method. A Low Pass filter was needed to remove high-frequency signals from the PWM base frequency. The system was made with source code design using two ways, the first source code used timerO and timerl directly while the second source code used the delay() and analogWrite() functions that had been provided by Arduino. From the research results, the output waveform had a sine shape and a frequency that was in accordance with the calculations at the time of software design. The use of dual low-pass filters could reduce/eliminate high-frequency signals originating from the PWM base frequency.

articleTitle: Extended Kit-Build Concept Mapping Tool to Facilitate Online Teaching and Learning in Post-COVID-19 Era
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Extended Kit-Build is an extension concept mapping tool that has been proven to improve student understanding. It provides an approach to broadening knowledge and enhancing meaningful learning. Several early studies have proven the positive effects of implementing the Extended Kit-Build. However, previous studies have focused on the impact of Extended Kit-Build on student achievement. There is no information regarding the suitability of the Extended Kit-Build to facilitate teaching and learning, particularly in the post-COVID-19 era. Therefore, the present study is intended to reveal the extent to which the extended kitbuild supports learning activities after the COVID-19 pandemic. Questionnaires of teachers and university students were involved in measuring their level of agreement. The results highlighted that the extended-kit-build could be applied to support post-covid-19 learning and teaching activities.

articleTitle: Students’ Response, Engagement, and Achievement of Gamification in Online Learning
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Increasing the efficiency, achievement, motivation, and involvement of students in e-learning can be achieved by utilizing gamification. Gamification is the use of elements related to video games (game mechanics and game dynamics) in non-game applications. This study aimed to analyze the students’ interest, engagement, and achievement in gamification in online learning. This study used a qualitative descriptive research method. The number of respondents was 66 students in the Technology Study Program of Makassar State University. The results of the study found that From the students’ responses to gamification obtained 98% stated fun in implementing gamification in online learning. The student engagement for overall materials in gamification found that students obtained 92% who said more able to engage the teaching materials by using gamification in online learning. And the students’ achievement for overall materials in gamification obtained 98% who said easy to understand the teaching materials by using gamification in online learning. It can be concluded that Gamification learning improves students’ response, engagement, and achievement. For the most part, students are essential participants in a productive learning process and, therefore, gamification techniques are critical to the effective completion of course requirements and involvement in online learning.

articleTitle: Study on Students’ Acceptance of Padlet as Online Discussion Medium
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Collaborative, active learning can enhance students’ comprehension of learning materials. Padlet usage during online learning can be a medium in which students collaboratively discuss in class. This study aims to observe students’ acceptance to Padlet usage as a medium for discussion in class. Respondents are students of 6th semester PGSD undergraduate program at Universitas Negeri Yogyakarta. The questionnaire consisted of 5 parameters measured using the Likert scale and 1 open-ended question that was analyzed using thematic analysis. This study found that Padlet is well-accepted by students. Padlet’s mind map templates and colorful appearance attracted students to use it. Internet signal and inconvenience of accessing using smart phone, as well as teachers’ lack of pedagogical capacity in using Padlet optimally are major challenges in the acceptance of Padlet by students. Further study is needed with more and wider participants, longer study duration, additional variables, such as teachers’ pedagogical capacity and resource identification students have for online learning.

articleTitle: Development of Web-Based E-Library with Open Source System for Elementary School
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Along with the development of learning technology, the existence of school libraries is now also increasingly optimized in the e-library. The results of the needs analysis show that there is a need for a special e-library design that can be used by schools efficiently to overcome the limitations of special library management personnel in schools. Based on this condition, this research is aimed at developing an e-library designed to be web-based with an open-source system. The research procedure is carried out referring to the ADDIE model with its data collection through questionnaires and documentation. The data from this study were processed with descriptive qualitative to describe the implementation of the developed system and descriptive quantitative to describe the results of expert validation of the feasibility of the e-library. The results showed that a web-based e-library with an open-source system was successfully developed and was suitable for use referring to the criteria of initiative, metadata, objects, and collections applied. The results of this development show that web-based e-libraries with open source systems can be used more practically and efficiently referring to administrative management features, book isolation, and visitor access for the elementary school level.

articleTitle: Assessing The Learning Environment using A Digital Platform: Coffee Shop Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The learning environment has an important role in increasing motivation and comfort for students in the learning process. Without a sense of comfort in learning, the learning objectives will be difficult to achieve. Along with the times and the increasing number of phenomena that appear in society, the learning environment that is only centered in schools or formal classes is also shifting. Factors in the learning environment in schools include learning methods or strategies, class conditions, and learning atmosphere. In the learning environment, motivation has an important role in the learning process. In this case the author wants to raise the concept of a Coffee Shop learning environment that is able to present a pleasant learning atmosphere so that students feel comfortable. Nowadays, the community seems to make the Coffee Shop a place to do various things, such as doing assignments, even to discuss, and the Coffee Shop phenomenon has developed into a modern society lifestyle. The concept of the Coffee Shop learning environment is also supported by local and national potentials where Indonesia is one of the largest coffee-producing countries in the world.

articleTitle: The Effect of Game-Based Application in Improving Students’ Engagement towards Learning Malay Language in Primary School
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)

authors.preferredName: Mohd Nihra Haruzuan Bin Mohamad Said

abstract: Game-based applications play a significant role in improving student engagement in lessons in this era of globalisation. The purpose of this study was to see if the game-based application (Wordwall) could help students become more engaged in the Malay Language. The main focus is on the effect of game-based application (Wordwall) in learning Malay Language, which is based on four factors, such as behavioural engagement, cognitive engagement, psychological engagement and academic engagement. Furthermore, the study investigates the relationship between the Year 4 pupils' overall performance before and after using game-based learning through Wordwall application in Malay Language and the influence of game-based application (Wordwall) towards learning Malay Language. Pre and posttests, questionnaire, and student engagement instrument were used to conduct quantitative research on 33 respondents who were Year 4 students at a school in Batu Pahat district. The findings indicated there were significant differences between the mean of the pre-test scores and post-test scores for the Malay language achievement test, whereby results showed that students' engagement increased after the Wordwall application. Meanwhile, students expressed positive perceptions about the Wordwall application, stating that it has created an enjoyable learning environment in the classroom.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Weighted Product Method in the Tri Pramana-Based Formative-Summative Evaluation Application
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The main purpose of this research was to show the percentage level of the simulation results effectiveness of Weighted Product calculation in the Tri Pramana-based Formative-Summative evaluation application for evaluating e-learning. The approach of this research was a development that focused on simulation activities for the calculation of the Weighted Product method. The subjects involved in conducting simulations and effectiveness tests were ten experts, including five education evaluation experts and five informatics experts. The tool used for the effectiveness test by the expert was in the form of a questionnaire consisting of six questions related to the Weighted Productmethod. The technique of analyzing the results of data collection was quantitative descriptive. The research results showed that the effectiveness of the calculation simulation of the Weighted Product method was 93% so it was included in the category of excellence. The impact of this research on the field of education is the existence of new knowledge for evaluators about the importance of calculation simulation of the decision support system method used in evaluation applications in the field of education.

articleTitle: Evaluation of User Experience on the Augmented Reality Glovic Cafe and Bakery Jember Application to Maximize User Experience
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Technological developments increasingly support the design and implementation of more interactive learning media in the field of education, one of which is the use of augmented reality (AR) technology. The conditions and situation of the Covid-19 pandemic are also increasingly making education digital and online. The more various kinds of applications are developed, the more they must evaluate the user experience of the appearance and function of the application. Measurement of user experience in applications can use the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) tool, with 26 questionnaire points. The UEQ Quality results show that the Attractiveness scale is 2.04, the Pragmatic Quality scale is 1.68, and the Hedonic Quality scale is 1.17 which shows positive evaluation results, which means that it can be concluded that users tend to like the application in terms of user experience. Based on this data, users have used similar applications, and the updates are still lacking. The scales that show well are attractiveness, perspicuity, efficiency, and stimulation. From the results of the respondent’s data processing, it was concluded that the convenience of using the application was good enough from the user’s perception. The data also showed that the user enjoyed the application.

articleTitle: AHP Learning Website Development with The RAD Method for Deaf Student
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The learning target is to implement character education that is integrated with technology so that it can improve the quality of human resources. Learning using the website can be used for students, especially deaf students because learning is fun and there is a high element of creativity that makes it easier to remember learning material. This shows that education is starting to realize the need for a website to increase effectiveness and efficiency, especially for deaf students. This study develops a website-based learning application for deaf students. The material raised is AHP (Analytical Hierarchy Process) in the course of forecasting techniques. The material was chosen because based on a previous survey if the course is one of the subjects that is quite difficult. The application development method uses Rapid Application Development. The trial was conducted on media and material experts as well as 6 deaf students. Both trials produced good test results and were included in the valid and very good categories. Website-based applications do not get major revisions. Thus, this application is feasible to use.

articleTitle: Exploring the Habit of using Online Learning Platforms for Higher Order Thinking Skills with Data Mining Techniques
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Following the rise of information technology, the development of learning in the twenty-first century is accelerating (IT). To measure higher-order thinking skills (HOTS) using technology, it is necessary to be able to examine and evaluate the learning process However, the pursuit of HOTS can occasionally result in brand-new issues, such as anxiety and despair brought on by thoughts of failure. Using online learning techniques is thought to help people overcome their fear of failing. The purpose of this study is to assess the demand for HOTS in online learning activities in the twenty-first century. About 145 teachers of varying ages were participants in this study. Gender, age range, and years of teaching experience make up the demographic information about teachers. According to the study’s findings, most teachers favor the use of HOTS when implementing online learning activities. Additionally, digital modules, PowerPoint presentations, and other kinds of media are used to create online learning services that are available to assist in the development of HOTS. The application of the study’s findings can be created for evaluation in the deployment of 21st-century-appropriate learning and online learning methodologies.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Concentration Levels in Learning Using Zoom Meeting by Applying the Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) Method and Support Vector Machine (SVM) Classification
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The online learning system is one of the implementations of distance education through a learning system, an application that is widely used during distance learning is Zoom Meeting. This research was conducted to find out how effective the use of the Zoom Meeting application is for online learning. This study focuses on detecting eyes to determine a person’s focus during online learning using zoom meetings, analyzing a person’s blink of an eye, and then determining the size of the ratio in the eyes. It has been established that the level of attention of a normal person can be determined by the degree of a blink of an eye. If a person feels tired or out of focus, it can be seen in the blink of his eyes. In this study, a method will be developed that is used to detect eyes using a Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as the extraction of its characteristics and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) as its classification. Base on data analysis proved that the ability of the process to identify a person’s focus level is 99.59% accuracy, 99.49% accuracy, and 98.84% recall. The system’s skills to detect blinking eyes with PERCLOS is excellent with an average 98.60%.

articleTitle: Measuring Student’s School Engagement in Blended Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The development of technology in the last decades made blended learning implemented wider, especially in the covid-19 pandemic last years. Online learning activities has some new issue to be defined. One of them is the difficulty of school engagement (disengagement). School counselors have the role of supporting student development tasks to avoid student disengagement. This research aims to measure the students’ school engagement, especially in the blended learning context. This research design used a quantitative survey. Research subjects include students in the city of Malang. The instrument used is the school engagement inventory. The study results indicate that students with mid-levels of school engagement have slightly more numbers than students with high levels of school engagement. Support engagement is a finding in this study as the specific aspect of engagement in the blended learning model. The suggestion is a more practical assessment of the demographic conditions of students to test and get a more appropriate construct of support engagement.

articleTitle: Designing GeoGebra Applet of Coordinate System for Fifth Graders: A Preliminary Study
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Learning media is a component for visualizing mathematics learning materials for students in elementary schools. This study aims to develop the GeoGebra applet of coordinate system material for fifth-grade elementary school students. The research was conducted using a research and development method with a 4D development model. There are four stages of development: define, design, develop, and disseminate. The data collection technique used was a validation questionnaire and semi-structured interviews. Three experts carried out validation with the first validity result of 77.75% (valid). After revisions, the second stage of the validation process was carried out with a second validity result of 93.65% (very valid). Then, the study was tested with three fifth-grade students, and the results showed that the students had a positive attitude toward using the GeoGebra applet. Therefore, the GeoGebra applet of coordinate system material for fifth-grade elementary school students is feasible to be used in the learning process.

articleTitle: Construction of Audio-Visual Elements Redundancy in Online Learning Materials As Learning Content
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This development research was conducted to reconstruct the richness and information density of learning content through redundancy in audio-visual elements in Sipejar (Learning Management System at Universitas Negeri Malang). The results of the construction became the basis for the development concept of Sipejar. The development principle minimizes display but provides more content. The development resulted in the product scope being a minimalist learning environment. Redundancy is carried out by considering the cognitive load and redundancy arrangement of audio-visual elements in product development. The results of the development are used to compile learning media in Sipejar. The construction of audio-visual elements is measured from user ratings in the form of clarity, access, attractiveness. Meanwhile, content potential is measured based on explain, efficiency and interesting

articleTitle: The Effect of The Self-Regulated Learning with The Alef Education Platform to Improve the High-Order Thinking Skills in Elementary School
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Digital media has a role in learning mathematics. This study aims to determine whether the application of the self-regulated learning model with the Alef Education platform can improve the high-order thinking skills of elementary school students. The population in this study were seventh-grade students of Madrasah Tsanawiyah in the province of Bali. The sample was drawn by random clusters in stages of 324 students. Data were collected by tests. Testing the effectiveness of the HOTS test using the effect size test. Data were analyzed descriptively qualitatively and quantitatively. The implementation of the self-regulated learning model with the alef education platform can improve the high-order thinking skills of elementary school students in the Province of Bali with Es =0.83 including the criteria for high effectiveness. On the alef platform, there are interesting audiovisual learning videos, games, and tiered tests. The implication of this research is that the application of the self-regulated learning model with the alef education platform can improve the high-order thinking skills of elementary school students.

articleTitle: Intelligent Ventilation System for COVID-19 Prevention using the IoT and Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: COVID-19 can be spread through the air, caused by inhaling smaller droplets1 containing SARS-CoV-2 in an indoor environment. In particular, both people with symptoms and people without symptoms make many small droplets and respiratory droplets when they breathe, sneeze, cough, or speak. When these tiny droplets are exposed to the air around them, they can react with the particles (PM) and stay in the air for a long time. The survival period depends on various conditions, including the type of surface, temperature, and relative humidity. The ventilation system is one way to solve this problem. This research makes a significant contribution to the development of intelligent ventilation systems utilizing the Internet of Things (IoT) and decision tree algorithms. The function of this system is to get a clean room environment from viruses by spraying disinfectant automatically and controlling the temperature and humidity of the air. Based on the results of this study, the system is able to control and categorize room conditions based on temperature and humidity factors. The classification value using the C4.5 decision tree algorithm is 92.33% with an average temperature and humidity value of 25oC and 49%.

articleTitle: Web and iOS-based Instant Messaging (IM) Application for Educational Institution with Limited Internet Access Regions
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The development of communication technology through smartphone has made real time communication (chat) faster, easier, and cheaper for educational institutions, especially between students and lecturers. This study aims to develop an architecture for Web and iOS-based instant messaging (IM) application and implement it into educational institutions in limited internet access regions according to its conditions and needs as a fast, easy, efficient, and effective communication and to support the lecture operations. Data collection method in this study is carried out by distributing questionnaire to lecturers and students. The IM development method is by using the Rational Unified Process (RUP). XMPP protocol is implemented into architecture and IM is developed with features of private chat, class-grouping based chat, broadcast message, scheduled message, and file attachment. This IM can accelerate the delivery of information from educational institutions to or between students and lecturers.

articleTitle: Field Trials of Discrepancy Evaluation Application Based on Tat Twam Asi-TOPSIS
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Field trials are very important to do to determine the effectiveness of an application that is applied in the field. This study aimed to show the percentage of effectiveness level of the Tat Twam Asi-TOPSIS-based Discrepancy Evaluation Application through field trials. This study approach was the development research by a development model referring to Borg & Gall. The study focus was only on field trials and revisions. The location of this study was carried out at several IT vocational schools in Bali. The subjects involved in the field trials were 54 respondents. Data collection tool in the form of a questionnaire consisting of 14 questions. The technique used to analyze the study data was descriptive quantitative, by comparing the field trials results with the effectiveness standard which refers to a scale of eleven. The study results showed that the average percentage of the effectiveness level of the evaluation application was 87.487, so it was categorized as very good. The impact of the study results on the fields of computer science and education is to raise awareness of the importance of field trials being conducted to determine the effectiveness of an evaluation application.

articleTitle: Meaningful Online Learning with e-Portfolio: University Students’ Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Emergency online classes can put students’ engagement at risk as the learning setting limits interaction, motivation, and understanding of the lesson, unlike the preCovid-19 times, when students can meet their instructors and peers face-to-face. Consequently, an innovative approach is needed to achieve successful and meaningful learning. This study seeks to Figure out students’ perspectives on e-portfolio projects. The researcher set out this topic based on a pre-research showing students’ low performance and engagement, hence the use of classroom action research (CAR) as the research method. After one cycle was conducted, the researcher focused on revealing students’ perceptions of the e-portfolio project. The survey responses indicated a successful implementation of meaningful learning: the students exhibited active participation, critical and creative thinking, problem-solving skill, and teamwork. The project also proved that students were engaged in the learning process while utilizing digital technology.

articleTitle: Personalized Recommendation of Study Materials Based on Automatic Short Answer Scoring Results
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The results of automatic short answer scoring (ASAS) can be used to provide learning recommendations. However, previous studies on ASAS are focused on the quality of the scoring method, without considering giving feedback on the student performance in the exam sessions. Moreover, research on feedback in the learning activity is more concentrated on creating an adaptive learning process. Therefore, this study aims to combine the Automatic Short Answer Scoring method and an Automatic Recommendation System to create an adaptive feedback system that has the ability to personalize the recommendation of study materials for the student based on their exam result. This study uses a dataset of ten questions, including one reference answer per question. The experiment result shows the recommendation system gives the maximum similarity score at 0.8972, with the maximum average score for all questions is 0.801. Future studies may continue to examine a technique for automatically generating study materials from various resources.

articleTitle: The Effect of Hybrid Learning Strategy and Achievement Motivation on Student Learning Outcomes
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Online learning has become a central element in the discussion in universities. Many institutes and universities are starting to offer online classes as an alternative to face-to-face learning. Hybrid learning (HL) is a pedagogical approach that combines face-to-face meetings (F2F) with technology or computer-assisted learning. The purpose of this study was to find out the effect of implementing a hybrid learning strategy on the learning outcomes of students who have high and low achievement motivation. Data analysis used the 2x2 factorial ANOVA (Analysis of Variance) statistical method for learning outcomes. The results of ANOVA on testing the influence of learning strategy factors on learning outcomes resulted in the value of F = 2.703 with sig = 0.104.

articleTitle: Face Recognition in Mobile-Based Test Systems Using FaceNet
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Almost all activities are currently implemented with applications, including the implementation of exams, especially the covid-19 pandemic has caused online exams to have begun to be widely used by various kinds of educational institutions, online exams are carried out generally using computer devices that require a lot of devices and space for infrastructure. This study aims to create an online exam system that is simple and easy to do by utilizing mobile devices. This system utilizes the face recognition feature for security and minimizes the occurrence of fraud. The method used is FaceNet taking an input image quality of 160x160 pixels with an accuracy percentage of 85.7%.

articleTitle: Assessment the Effectiveness of Using Websites for Principal Skills Training in Facilitating Freedom to Learn
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Now, there are many online course platforms available on the internet, but there is no online course website, which specifically offers courses or training related to improving the competence of principals, especially in the context of facilitating learning independence in schools. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of training websites for school principals in facilitating freedom to learn in school. This study uses a descriptive quantitative research design, with three assessment criteria, namely display, display material and usefulness. The research respondents were 77 principals and teachers. The results of the study show that the effectiveness of the website is in the very good category, meaning that this website can already be used.

articleTitle: The Implications of Using Web-Based Diary Writing Apps as Innovative Learning for Writing Enforcement
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study discusses the implications of using web-based diary writing apps among university students to enforce writing intentions during the learning process in the post-pandemic era. There were ten university students, who were selected randomly, participating in this research study. Data were gathered through a collection of diary posts in the web-based diary writing app and an online survey using Google Forms distributed among participants. Then, data analysis employed descriptive qualitative analysis. The findings reveal that the web-based diary writing app provided technological implications for its users and aided their users to be more productive in writing in enjoyable conditions. Such implications may indicate that the web-based diary writing app served as innovative learning for university students since it integrated emojis and colors, a future version of emotional communication tools. Indeed, this research study designates the positive implications of web-based diary writing for enforcing the writing habits of university students.

articleTitle: Identification of Cybercounseling Services for Improving High School Students' Cultural Intelligence in Social Media
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: One of the positive impacts of technological developments is that there are no limits for someone to communicate. Freedom of expression causes students to forget to set boundaries when interacting with people who have different cultures when using social media. This sometimes causes friction or even intolerance related to SARA to become a common thing on social media. The purpose of this study is to identify high school students regarding the need for cybercounseling services such as what is needed to increase cultural intelligence in social media. The implementation of this research uses quantitative methods with the design of the research implementation using a survey. The data obtained were then analyzed descriptively with the aim of finding the basic needs of students. The results showed that most students agreed on the need for cybercounseling services for handling social media problems. Furthermore, that high school students tend to choose a website for the implementation of cybercounseling with the form of supporting media is a short video. The condition experienced by students in social media is that some students still cannot control themselves and have difficulty interacting with people of different cultures when using social media.

articleTitle: Emotion Recognition based on Heart Rate Detection using Logistic Regression for Automation Food Healing Application
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Daily pressure activity especially in work place or any society condition may causing stress or pressure for the people deal with that condition. This stress may causing of decreasing of work performance and achievement in the daily activity. Furthermore in worse condition, people may went to psychiatrist consulting regarding the condition in order to heal the stress or pressure feeling. In this work, food recommendation healing in order to improve the mood based on mood recognition using heartbeat rate detection system is developed. Mood detection results will be used to recommend foods that can improve the mood. the mood detection system work based on automatic intelligent heartbeat rate identification. This system installed on an Android cellphone, so its make the system more flexible and portable. the system has also connected to the web, in order used by doctors to monitor the patient's condition if the patient is being monitoring due to health mental diseases treatment. This system has worked properly with mood detection based on heartbeat rate with 96% and 97%, training and testing accuracy, respectively. Furthermore, this system is connected to the website for monitoring purposes for the psychiatrist to monitor their patient intern of mood changing fluctuation

articleTitle: Digital Technology Transformation and Empowerment of Technology: A New Paradigm of Classroom Management for an “Merdeka Belajar” Policy in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The purpose of this research is pertaining to digital transformation and technology empowerment; especially in the aspect of the new paradigm of classroom management for freedom learning policies in Indonesia. The research data were obtained and examined from educational figures who were closely related to the freedom learning paradigm. The characters in question are Carl Ransom Rogers, John Dewey, and Henry Armand Giroux. The analysis of the data was through Gadamer’s hermeneutic paradigm. Data interpretation comes from text, in the form of the work of the character in question. The study finds that the digital transformation and technology empowerment, especially in the aspect of the classroom management paradigm for the “Merdeka Belajar” policy in Indonesia, occur due to internal and external factors. The implications for classroom management are discussed further.

articleTitle: Assessing Validity and Reliability of an Instrument for Measuring Student Digital Leadership: Example from Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Digital leadership can be understood as a leadership strategy used by a leader in utilizing digital assets to achieve organizational goals. This study aims to assess the validity and reliability of students’ digital leadership scale. Students’ digital leadership constructs were measured by six dimensions and 22 items were constructed to assess students’ digital leadership constructs. An online questionnaire survey using Google Form was conducted on 258 students of Laboratory High School, Universitas Negeri Malang, Indonesia. Validity analysis using Pearson Product-Moment Correlation and reliability analysis using Cronbach’s Alpha. The results show that of the 22 items, there are 21 items that have a high level of validity and reliability. Finally, the discussion and research recommendations are presented.

articleTitle: Development of Virtual Classroom for Hybrid Live Teaching Mode
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study developed a virtual classroom for object-oriented programming courses for gamification activities in a hybrid live teaching mode in early 2022. The aim is to facilitate students who want to take gamification activities directly in class but cannot attend due to several reasons, especially uncertain conditions pandemic. This can be made possible by utilizing a web-based virtual learning environment application. Gather.town is a video-conferencing platform that provides a new experience than what is traditionally used. He provides a virtual classroom that is designed to resemble a real classroom with a 2D Graphics mode featuring avatar-based games. Utilization of proximity-based video conferencing offers interactions that resemble real conditions with 2D maps of classroom layouts. This paper aims to explore the experiences of students attending online by utilizing the virtual classroom to participate in offline teaching in the classroom. The survey was carried out during five sessions of meetings with different or the same students. The results show that students respond positively to the use of Gather.town during hybrid live teaching mode lectures. However, only more than half of the students agreed that the virtual classroom did not replace the real class in teaching gamification activities.

articleTitle: Automatic Item Generation with Reading Passages: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Automatic Item Generation (AIG) is a system to generate items/questions automatically with a model using computer technology. AIG can help teachers to provide questions in education assessments more efficiently. Currently, AIG is already implemented in various educational subjects. Based on the author’s knowledge, there are no review papers that discuss AIG with reading passages. Here we conduct a systematic literature review to provide a comprehensive review of AIG, especially AIG with reading passages. The research objective is to know about AIG approaches datasets, evaluations, and challenges. We use S phases: planning and managing the review, defining the research question, identifying inclusion and exclusion criteria, search strategy, screening titles and abstracts, selecting full-text paper, data extraction, analysis, and synthesis. This research reviewed 30 relevant papers between 201S and 2022. We found that various approaches have been implemented. An approach is not driven by what kind of language will be used in the generated question. On the other hand, dataset selection is always based on the question language and question type that will be generated. Before generated questions are used in assessment, it is necessary to evaluate the question quality. Despite the success stories above, AIG still has some challenges for future development.

articleTitle: Measuring the Effect of Midterm Exam on Final Exam of Online Learning during COVID-19 Pandemic: The Mediating Role of Assignments
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study measures the relationship between midterm exams, assignments, and final exams of online learning on university students during the COVID-19 pandemic. The research subjects were 206 students from six departments at the Faculty of Education, Universitas Negeri Malang. The data was obtained from the database of the Academic Information System of Universitas Negeri Malang. The results showed that the midterm exam had a significant effect on assignments, the midterm exam had a significant effect on the final exam, and the assignments had a significant effect on the final exam. The analysis shows that assignments significantly mediate the effect of the midterm exam on the final exam.

articleTitle: Image Classification of Decapterus Macarellus Using Ridge Regression
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Pelagic fish such as mackerel are a source of protein in Indonesia. However, there is no decapterus macarellus as an open dataset for image processing using various classification algorithms. Where its use includes the sensor-assisted sorting process in checking fresh fish and rotten fish. For this reason, this study aims to provide a classification model for pelagic fish and their primary datasets which is available for free on the IEEE data port. Artificial intelligence is used in the process of guided classification with the help of ground truth for the preparation of fish classes. The dataset used is a primary dataset consisting of fish images, arranged in two classes, namely 71 fresh fish and 96 rotten fish. The methods used are k-NN classifiers, naive bayes and ridge regression. Experiments were drawn up to classify rotten fish and fresh fish. The preprocessing was assisted by InceptionV3 as a feature extraction method. Furthermore, the image data is trained in a ratio of 60:40 for training and testing data. Validation was performed using 2-fold cross validation with the results obtained being 99.4%, 94% and 100% accuracy using the classifiers namely k-NN, naive bayes and ridge regression, respectively.

articleTitle: Interaction of Mobile Learning Media with Portfolio on Photography Material for Vocational High School Students
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Learning media is an important aspect of learning, especially with the Covid-19 pandemic encouraging the need for students to study online. Based on observations made in several vocational schools in Malang and Balikpapan, books or ppt are media used in learning. There has been no innovation in learning media in the field of sound and image processing technology. To develop interesting learning media and foster student creativity, a mobile learning media was developed using problem-based learning methods in photography and videography for class XI multimedia SMK students to increase student creativity. The R&D model used is Sadiman’s version of R&D as follows: 1)need assessment; 2)goal setting; 3)set of ingredient formulations; 4)development of success metrics; 5)Create media scripts; 6)inspection; 7)production ready; Validation was carried out by media experts and material experts, then analyzed using the User Experience Questionnaire (UEQ) method with quantitative and qualitative data types with questionnaire-based data collection methods and feasibility tests on students. The results of the study showed a score of 95.13% for material experts, and 84% for media experts and student creativity as measured by UEQ obtained a score of 76.75%. That is, the percentage has a very good meaning.

articleTitle: Development of Gamification in Education and Training of Nature Lovers Student organizations
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The low level of activity of MPA Jonggring Salaka members who participated in the “Division Rally” education and training program led to a review of one component of the education and training program, that component is curriculum. This study develops a gamified design of education and training program for members of MPA Jonggring Salaka. The purpose of this paper is to explain the development of gamification design of the MPA Jonggring Salaka education and training “Division Rally” program, as well as to see whether students will view this gamification positively or not. Based on a survey of the gamification development literature, this gamification development was designed using a game-based learning model by Rosemary Garris, where in this development there are three development stages, Input, Process, and Output. In this study, the gamification design was tested on 29 students to see their response to the gamification of education and training program that developed by the researcher. This survey data includes quantitative with Likert scale and qualitative with student comments. The results showed that the design of education and training programs received a positive response from students, because their hard work and learning felt rewarded by the existence of gamification.

articleTitle: Enhancing BIPA Students’ Listening Ability through the Implementation of the Audiobook E-learning Media
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The study aimed to determine the implementation of audiobook e-learning media in BIPA-Indonesian Language for Foreign Speakers-Xiangzhu class to enhance the student’s Indonesian listening ability. As stages of the research procedure, qualitative methods and the ADDIE approach were utilized to conduct the research. In addition, triangulation data was used in the analysis of the data. One class consisted of one lecturer, and twenty-one students participated in the research as participants. The result revealed that through the audiobook e-learning media implementation, which was carried out for four weeks, the student’s listening skills improved; they could distinguish sounds and understand the sentence structure. In addition, audiobook e-learning media materials have helped students comprehend the given material. It allowed them to understand the content, remember the material, use the material they heard as knowledge of the world of work, and comprehend specific terms related to the topic explained, such as job application letters, interviews, and some kinds of a business letter.

articleTitle: Teacher-Perceived Ubiquitous Learning Environment for Peer-to-Peer Collaborative Learning to Student Achievement
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study examines the effect of teacher perceptions of U-Learning learning on peer-to-peer collaborative learning on student achievement mediated by learning adaptation and academic self-efficacy. This study uses a quantitative approach with data obtained through a questionnaire. This research was conducted in an Elementary school in Malang city involving 66 students in grade 6. The data in this study, the data that has been obtained, is processed using path analysis assisted by smartPLS 3.0 applications. Based on the research findings, it is known that the teacher’s perception of the ubiquitous learning environment for peer-to-peer collaborative learning affects student achievement in elementary schools, selling academic efficacy and learning adaptation. Academic self-efficacy is known to mediate the relationship between teacher perceptions regarding U-Learning on students’ academic achievement and can also directly influence student achievement. Meanwhile, Learning adaptability can also mediate the relationship related to U-Learning on student academic achievement and can influence student achievement directly. Based on the research findings, teachers should also provide learning by involving the child’s closest environment so that the media involved is not only electronic media but also authentic objects.

articleTitle: Implementation “TRINGO” Philosophy for Multi Literations’ Digital Learning Design
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study aims to develop a Tringo-based multiliteracy learning design in learning to write exposition texts. The research method used is research and development, while the Dick and Carrey development model is the development model used. In this research and development, it is only limited to the expert validation test stage due to research limitations. Learning tools that become the output of this learning design are lesson plans (RPP), student worksheets (LKPD), learning e-modules and guidelines for using learning designs. The results of the development of this learning design were validated by material experts and media experts with the average number of all devices developed obtaining a percentage of 89.76%. The testing phase for students was carried out with individual trials, scoring 89%, small group trials of 81%, and field trials of 89%. The results of the validation and testing on the students showed that the learning design developed was feasible or valid to be used in the learning process and got a good response from the students.

articleTitle: Translated-Webcomics as an Arabic Translation Learning Medium
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Arabic translation learning is essential because translation activities require mastery of various theories and experiences. However, the media used in Arabic translation learning activities have not been widely studied and developed. In fact, in this modern era, many media have the potential to be good media to use in learning Arabic translation, one of which is webcomics. This study aims to explore the potential of webcomics as a medium that can be used in Arabic translation learning and to show how to use it in Arabic translation learning activities. This conceptual research uses a literature review and comparative case studies on webcomics in various learning activities. The results of this study indicate that webcomics can be used as a medium for learning and evaluation in Arabic translation learning.

articleTitle: Primary School Teachers’ Motivation and Creativity in Creating Instructional Video: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Video design is an important competency that teachers need to integrate technology into learning and teaching. However, the model of design is still limited. This study aims to implement a learning video design model. It involved 43 teachers from 24 primary school institutions. The implementation method was conducted in stages from preprogram, preparation, design, editing, presentation, and evaluating. Data were collected by survey techniques, open-ended questions, and documentation. The results showed that before the training the teacher made an adjustment learning video with the lesson plan. The storyboard design step was highly accepted as the integration of planning into the learning video. The ease, functionality, and attitude of the teacher towards the steps of instructional video design also showed high scores. The implication of this training is that the model can be applied to video training for elementary school teacher.

articleTitle: An Android Application Based On Mental Health Moderated by Counseling: An Experimental Study For Mothers With Single Parent Status
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The family is the main center of role models for children. The mentally unstable condition of the single mother can also affect the child's development. This study used qualitative research with a quasi-experimental model and a pretest-post-test nonequivalent group method. Participants in this study were 60 single mothers aged 19-40 years who focused on Malang City. The sampling technique used is Total Sampling. The experimental procedure is structured in four steps. The study's results on the effectiveness of the Mental Health-Based Android application and mental health in the application moderated by counseling services showed a significant difference of 0.05, so counseling services for single mothers positively influenced maternal mental health.

articleTitle: Usability Testing of Emotion Recognition Assistance Application for Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: One of the problems faced by children with autism spectrum disorders (ASD) is the deficit to understand other people's emotions. This problem has an impact on the inability of ASD children to understand other people's feelings, interweave the relation, and the ability to empathize. This study aims to conduct usability testing of the Emotion Recognition Assistance application, which was developed to assist teachers in introducing basic emotional expressions. Ten children who were diagnosed with ASD were between the ages of 10 to 20 years as a respondent in this study. This study concludes that the Emotion Recognition Assistance application has proven to be effective in terms of convenience of use and legibility of application content, and not effective in terms of the ease of use of the application. Children with autism spectrum disorders need prerequisite skills, that is understand simple instructions to be able to learn to recognize emotional expressions using this application.

articleTitle: A Four Tier Web Based Assessment with Eight Categories Diagnostic
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The study aims to develop a web-based assessment to diagnose students’ abilities through the four-tier test (FTDT). The development has three stages: design, development, and testing. Tests are conducted sequentially by expert assessment and field testing. Field testing was conducted in 10 schools representing three school clusters. The results of the expert assessment were analyzed using minifac (facets Rasch), while the field tests were analyzed descriptively. The results prove the feasibility of FTDT web-based assessment as a measuring and diagnostic tool. Testing on 743 students confirmed the accuracy and reliability of the FTDT web-based assessment. The diagnostic results show that students in high clusters are better than in middle and low cluster schools, with the highest achievement being the decision Lack of Knowledge type 2. The responses from teachers and students regarding the use of FTDT web-based assessment have implications that socialization is needed to learn more about the objectives and outputs of the diagnostic test.

articleTitle: Cognitive Assessment of Students Using Testing Instruments on Computer Networks Courses in Informatics and Computer Engineering Education Study Program at UNJ
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study aims to design an assessment instrument to assess students' cognition in computer networking lessons. The design and design of the test instrument followed the ADDIE model, from the analysis stage to determine student targets and characteristics, then the design stage, determining learning objectives, learning material design, and question grids, at this stage the number of Subject Matter Experts (SME) was also determined as many as 6 people, for 6 Subject Matter Experts (SME), the minimum acceptable Content Validation Ratio (CVR) is 0.99, while the Content Validation Index (CVI) is 0.83. At the development stage, 81 items were designed as a draft assessment instrument. At the implementation stage, the Subject Matter Experts (SME) assessed each item on the draft assessment instrument. This study uses a quantitative content validity approach from the Lawshe model with a 3-point scale as follows: essential, useful but not necessary, and non-essential. Each Subject Matter Expert (SME) was given an instrument to assess each item in the test instrument. The Subject Matter Expert (SME) will determine whether an important question is given, normal or normal, or whether the question is not important given to students. At the evaluation stage, the Subject Matter Expert (SME) assessment of the draft test instrument will be compiled and the Content Validation Ratio (CVR) value and the Content Validation Index (CVI) value calculated to determine content validity.

articleTitle: Gender Role in Turn-taking: A Case Study of EFL Online Classroom in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study aims at investigating the role of gender in online classroom turn-taking. Since the Covid-19 pandemic turned the traditional classroom into an online interaction, the communication strategy of teaching-learning suddenly moved. The face-to-face classroom activity has twisted into textual computer-mediated communication. This sudden shift also influences EFL students’ contact with their teachers and other students. Therefore, the discourse exchange from 4 online higher education classrooms was collected and analyzed to see how gender influences the participants’ turn-taking process in an online classroom. The result revealed that the teacher selection occurred more on the teachers’ side. However, the female students took more turns compared to the male student. This finding concludes that gender role still becomes one of the fruitful discussions within classroom interaction. In the end, it is hoped that this issue’s finding could be an insightful input for the teacher to create more interactive classes for both male and female students.

articleTitle: Emerging Hybrid Online Learning in Post-pandemic Situation: Idealism and Reality
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The Covid-19 pandemic has significantly changed the way of learning models, one of which is the implementation of hybrid online learning (HOL). Although some instructors have applied this model to their learning activities, the process and results are still not optimal due to various constraints. Therefore, this paper explores HOL implementation regarding its idealism and reality in post-pandemic situations where face-to-face (F2F) learning is allowed in limited circumstances. For this reason, a descriptive-analytical systematic review of the relevant papers discusses the implementation of learning with the HOL model and is relied upon in this study to draw the reality of its implementation and offer solutions to potential problems. The investigation shows that many instructors have tried to apply this learning model because it is considered very suitable in post-pandemic situations to facilitate students who can attend face-to-face (F2F) in classrooms and for those who choose to be in a different room but still need to keep interacting synchronously with the other participants in the classroom. However, this learning model is considered not optimal in the real situation, both regarding the learning process and achievement of expected learning outcomes, due to several technical and non-technical obstacles.

articleTitle: Development of MOOC and SIPEJAR Learning Media through Animated Video Simulation of Instructional Supervision
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: The development of information and communication technology has an influence on the learning process within educational institutions. The selection of the right and interesting learning media can affect students’ motivation in attending lectures. This study aims to develop MOOC and SIPEJAR learning media through animated videos conducted in instructional supervision courses through the Project Based Learning (PjBL) model. The method used in this research is the development research method. The development is carried out on online learning media by making simulation videos of animation-based instructional supervision. The result of this study is the production of online learning videos through animation-based videos of eight animated videos following the topics of instructional supervision lecture materials. The results of the development of this online learning video have been tested on students with excellent results.

articleTitle: Digital News Transformation on Education in the Most Affected Country by COVID-19 Using the Topic Modeling and Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study focuses on examining US newspaper articles regarding education from the two major news channels the New York Times (NYT) (N=29.682) and Washington Post (WST) (N=44.308) in period 1 January, 2020 - 19 March, 2021, and splitting them into three stages. We employed Latent Dirichlet Allocation topic modeling and sentiment analysis to depict the overall picture of the data set. Our method flow chart included start, data preparing, data analysis, and result. We used Python to call Google API to calculate the sentiment analysis score. There is a difference in the frequency of the occurrences of the education theme in NYT and WST in the three stages, where NYT relatively dominates. Keywords related to education that appear on the NYT and WST include school, child, parent, student, child, family, feel, and home. Sentiment analysis scores on all themes in NYT and WST were generally in the neutral categories, while the direction from stage one to stage three tends to be more positive. This study could be useful to assist education policy makers in determining the right decisions in the implementation of quality education after the COVID-19 Pandemic era.

articleTitle: Development of a Technology-Based Parenting Support Center Model to Support Stunting Reduction Programs
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This research aims to produce a valid, effective, and practical technology-based parental support center model for reducing stunting rates. The research and development (R& D) method is used in this research. The trial was conducted on 1062 participants of the Toddler Family Development program from 40 Toddler Family Development groups in the Klojen District, so a sample of291 Toddler Family Development program participants was obtained in Klojen District, Malang City. The study results indicate that the model of childcare services through mobile applications developed as a whole is in the excellent or decent category. This is based on the assessment results, with 82.36% from the media and 76.54%. From a material expert. This shows that the technology-based parental support center model in supporting stunting reduction programs is well developed or feasible. The application also received an assessment from parents of 81.54%. Using this application can be a milestone in the birth of an information system. This can minimize data processing errors. Report delays so that problems related to problems can be minimized to a minimum, and help mothers of toddlers understand stunting during child development. The development of this stunting information system is beneficial in overcoming problems related to entering and reporting data accurately, precisely, quickly, and correctly.

articleTitle: Developing ESP-Based CLIL to Increase Students’ Engagement in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: This study aims at addressing the need for a private institution to have a better English for Specific Purposes (ESP) course that can help students to navigate their professional lives as academicians and as future professionals in the field of Visual Communication Design. To achieve the goal, a series of lesson plans along with material and the assessment was developed using Borg & Gall’s (2002) research and development cycle: (1) need analysis, (2) development stage, (3) expert validation, (4) try out. As a result, the entire lesson was designed to promote collaborative work through jigsaw and the active production of the target language. CLIL was found appropriate because it boosted students’ enthusiasm to learn the language, particularly in a synchronous online class using Zoom, where students need to be more motivated to actively participate. ESP specialists have validated the lesson design and all teaching materials before implementation. The majority of students responded positively to the lesson as the CLIL method brought them closer to their discipline while also allowing them to study L2 to assist their performance in their discipline and future careers.

articleTitle: Design and Development of “Fright Hour” A Horror Game Utilizing Unreal Engine 5
publicationTitle: 2022 8th International Conference on Education and Technology (ICET)
abstract: Playing games is an activity that has several purposes such as finding entertainment facilities, filling spare time, and sometimes being used as a means of education. Games can be created using various types of Game Engine Software. Unreal Engine 5 is one of the Software Engines used to create Game products. The author will make a game titled “Fright Hour” based on Windows with the survival horror genre made with Unreal Engine 5 technology. The method used in the manufacture and design of this game is the Game Development Life Cycle, it consists of six phases: initiation, pre-production, production, testing, beta, and release. The authors also use an evaluation method called cognitive walkthrough where this method is used to evaluate problems that occur when players are testing games. This game was successfully developed using Game Development Life Cycle. The results of the cognitive walkthrough test were successful in identifying the problems in the game.
